description: The >N-row Markov weights are EXACTLY zero on the computed route (y_lambda_su_n) at every n from 2 to 9 — structural, since a Schur function of a shape with more rows than variables vanishes identically. The residues qou-e9le tracks are on the cached route.

data.cached_route: wedderburn_jones_markov._load_y_lambda_at_q0_witness → y-lambda-at-q0.witness.json (solver output; carries ~1e-73 residues — the qou-e9le trap)
data.computed_route: y_lambda_su_n → schur_principal (structural zero: a Schur function of a shape with more rows than variables vanishes identically)

assertion_notes.note: (n = 2..9, 67 over-row shapes in total; `v == 0`, not 'below tolerance')
(checked across n deliberately — an n=3-only check would not be evidence, as qbeta_rank_one_identity_is_n3_only_probe showed)
(1 at n=3 -> 25 at n=9, so the result is not carried by a near-empty set)

data.verdict: The qou-e9le trap is a property of the CACHED route, not of the weights. `_load_y_lambda_at_q0_witness` reads solver output, so a provably-zero weight arrives as a ~1e-73 residue and defeats a None/truthiness prune. The COMPUTED route `y_lambda_su_n` evaluates `schur_principal` directly, and a Schur function of a shape with more rows than variables is identically zero — measured at N = 2 for n = 2..9, every one of 67 over-row shapes is exactly `0.0`, not below-tolerance. So the sibling's row-count remedy is right and stays the safe general fix (a consumer cannot tell which route its `y` came from), but the affected producers also have the option of a route on which a truthiness check is already correct. Checked across n on purpose: a single-n check would not have been evidence. NOT claimed: that the cached witness is wrong — its residues move no number.
